observation: Make-the-bad-state-unrepresentable: the founder's load-bearing rejection (no pins / no drift) became an architecture invariant. usePicker exposes only HTMLElement refs; rects exist only inside useElementRect ('there is no rect in the engine to go stale'). Two design-critique CRITICALs about frozen-box drift drove this structurally — the rejected state is impossible to express, not merely guarded. SUPERSEDES-PROTOTYPE annotations made it auditable vs the prototype's {target,rect}. Fewer states to test, fewer to regress. Protect this pattern: when a founder rejects a failure mode, prefer an invariant that makes it unrepresentable over a runtime guard.

Live-proof on :8098 caught two geometry defects jsdom structurally cannot: (1) rail header/arm button sat under the viewer Toolbar and the theme/density pills intercepted the arm click (task-11 top:48px fix); (2) held box gluing through scroll + rail collapse/expand proven with measured deltas (elD100/boxD100). Review explicitly routed AC2/AC3 geometry + AC7 scroll + AC15 real-POST to live and named jsdom's blind spot (gBCR=0, scrollIntoView no-op, no layout). Division of labor (AC1-14 logic in jsdom, geometry to live) is the correct shape for a DOM-geometry feature.

Critique ran in parallel with the founder's human-design-review. Design-critique landed ~4 min after the design commit, architecture-critique ~3 min after the arch commit. The reviewer persona did not block on founder review; the two evaluation streams overlapped, compressing the critical path. Whole run (concept->docs) was ~1h36m, 11 commits, single session, zero pipeline-toolchain churn (no rebases/CI loops/attestation thrash). Concept locking the domain (no new primitive, additive optional anchor) + naming the AJ5 wiring bug up front as build task #1 = clean spec, green-first-pass on logic ACs, 0 spec-mismatch defects at review.

Embodiment-story-lifecycle (4th+ occurrence): design-gate fixture story AnnotatorV2.stories.tsx (763 lines, 3 variants) rendered as a real catalog component (module count 60). Had to be deleted at Phase 5 + snapshot re-blessed (60->59, one obsolete VariantADevtoolsRail entry, 79 deletions). Same class as AJ6 CatalogAxis, W2 token-gallery, AJ5 overlay-mockups. The AJ6-proposed mitigation (plan names fixture + deletion trigger; code review verifies deletion) worked here (clean removal) but is still manual every run. Ripe for /compound — recurring + has a known-good mitigation that could be enforced.

Founder hit a BLANK annotator during the interactive run: multiple viewers fighting for fixed port 8098 across worktrees; a stale shadow from a DIFFERENT worktree's viewer was served, so the annotator opened unwired. Environment friction (dev-server state), not a code defect, but cost a confused round-trip. Recurs: AJ6 stale discovery.js shadow, AJ5 viewer-state. Candidate mitigation: per-worktree port derivation, or a pre-live-proof 'is this MY worktree's viewer?' probe before the founder/agent opens :8098.

AJ7 never registered in pipeline-manifest.yaml (grep AJ7 in .pipeline/work-packages returns nothing). 15 ACs self-authored against concept+approved-design, not traced to an upstream workpackage spec. Architecture-critique flagged it (CC-007 reconcile cannot run; no external AC source). Founder-directed dev-tool follow-ups skip /work-planning -> no manifest/track row -> /review, /retro, CC-007 lose their AC spine. This retro had to reconstruct the run from progress JSON + git history because plan artifacts were retired in Phase 5. Candidate: a lightweight 'register concept+approved-design pair as the spec' stub even for delegated runs.

Critique-resolution-not-implemented: arch-critique WARNING (element-unmount-while-held -> useElementRect returns gBCR all-zeros -> 0x0 ghost box at viewport origin) was named in the critique, ACCEPTED in the plan resolution (prose: 'treat !el.isConnected as null'), but NOT implemented in the build. Code review caught it as SF-2; fix-loop closed it (useElementRect !isConnected->null + usePicker MutationObserver clears held el on detach). Signal: a critique resolution recorded in prose is not a guarantee it lands in code. Candidate: code review should trace each accepted critique resolution to a concrete code site, not just to the plan.

In-flight founder cleanup interleaved with the pipeline: dead density-switcher removal (dc9c6bb6, separate MEMORY project_density_removal task, 58 deletions) committed between review-fix and docs ON the AJ7 branch. Review correctly scoped it OUT of AJ7 (pre-exists on origin/main) but it now rides AJ7's PR. Mild scope-bleed from the interactive run; harmless but muddies the PR story. Note in PR body. Pattern: interactive runs accrete unrelated founder cleanups onto the feature branch.

Delegated human-design-review: the novel-design hard gate was CLEARED by founder delegation ('anything that doesn't occlude the components works') rather than the annotate-in-browser->revise-TSX loop. Worked here (no-occlusion became a binding principle and drove SF-1 rail-reflow), but the gate's intended artifact (browser annotations driving TSX revisions) was skipped. Worth tracking how often the novel-design gate is delegated vs exercised, and whether delegation needs a recorded binding-principle so downstream review can check against it (it did here: 'no-occlusion' was checkable).
